title: German Language – Level 02
overview: German Language – Level 02 develops elementary German communication skills for learners who have completed introductory study or demonstrate equivalent proficiency. The course builds accuracy and confidence in everyday exchanges, extends control of core sentence structures and verb forms, and develops listening, speaking, reading, and writing through realistic personal, social, travel, and workplace situations. Guided practice emphasizes understandable communication, appropriate register, and independent use of familiar German.
audience: Learners who have completed German Language – Level 01 or possess equivalent foundational knowledge.
Students and professionals seeking stronger everyday German communication skills.
Travelers, residents, and individuals preparing for routine interactions in German-speaking environments.
Learners progressing toward higher-level German language study.
methodology: Interactive communicative lessons combining brief grammar explanations, modeled dialogues, pair and group speaking activities, pronunciation practice, guided listening, short reading tasks, structured writing, vocabulary recycling, and situational role-plays. Formative quizzes, teacher feedback, self-assessment, and an integrated final performance task monitor progress across the four language skills.
competencies: Elementary spoken interaction and turn-taking in familiar contexts.
Comprehension of short, clearly delivered everyday German messages.
Use of common present, past, and future-oriented expressions.
Accurate basic sentence construction, questions, negation, and word order.
Reading practical notices, short messages, and simple informational texts.
Writing connected short messages and descriptions using appropriate vocabulary.
Cultural awareness and polite communication in everyday situations.
objectives: Exchange information about routines, preferences, past activities, and near-future plans.
Ask and answer questions using common interrogative forms and appropriate sentence order.
Use essential modal verbs, separable verbs, and common past-tense patterns in context.
Understand the main points of short conversations, announcements, and instructions.
Describe people, places, experiences, and everyday problems with increasing detail.
Read and respond to short emails, notices, schedules, and practical information.
Write brief connected texts, invitations, requests, and descriptions.
Participate in routine shopping, travel, appointment, and workplace interactions.
